job.title: Senior Legal Counsel - Employment & Litigation
job.description:
Our client is a large, well-established organisation operating in a complex and highly regulated environment. An opportunity has arisen for an adaptable, commercially minded Employment Lawyer with experience in workplace law and dispute resolution to join their highly regarded in-house Legal team on a 12-month contract basis, working alongside experienced employment and litigation specialists.

As part of a high-performing and collaborative legal function, you will provide expert legal advice on a wide range of employment, industrial relations, and workplace matters. Key responsibilities include advising on employment contracts, performance management, termination, workplace health and safety, diversity, and compliance with modern awards and enterprise agreements. You will also manage and advise on pre-litigation matters and disputes before courts and industry bodies, including advocacy where required, and provide input on collective bargaining and industrial instrument interpretation. The role also includes managing external counsel and attending mediations and conciliations.

You will be a versatile senior lawyer with 6+ years’ PQE and strong expertise in employment and workplace law and dispute resolution. Experience advising on complex regulatory and contentious matters is essential, alongside a pragmatic, solutions-focused approach. Confident working independently in a fast-paced commercial environment, you will bring sound judgment and the ability to build trusted relationships across a wide range of stakeholders. The position would suit a Senior Associate seeking their first move in-house, or an existing in-house lawyer looking to build their employment and litigation experience.

Our client offers a highly flexible environment with hybrid working, including two days a week in the office, and is open to a four or five day a week arrangement. Melbourne based.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact Sarah Ling on 0402 265 217. Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.

job.title: Senior Financial Accountant
job.description:
This is an exciting opportunity to join a progressive and highly successful Australian business which provides a market leading portfolio of products and services to institutional clients and consumers across the globe. The business is committed to remaining at the forefront of its industry and is internationally renowned for its innovative approach to product design, superior service delivery and customer care.

Reporting to a Finance Manager and as a key member of a collegial head office team you will primarily be responsible for managing the day-to-day accounting and month end reporting requirements for a number of entities within the Group. You will be expected to take the lead in investigating and resolving transaction queries by working collaboratively with stakeholders across the broader business, support the timely completion of periodic management reports for the Group Consolidation and help to ensure that the business meets its external statutory reporting and taxation compliance obligations. Proactive, curious and hands on you will also be expected to use your accounting subject-matter-expertise to continuously improve financial processes and systems and also help to maintain and develop an internal control framework which effectively meets the ongoing requirements of a growing international business.

This highly engaging role is likely to appeal to a qualified CA or CPA who is seeking to continue their professional development within an evolving and supportive Group Finance function of an international business. You have probably already worked in a similar multi-entity corporate environment (ideally with some exposure to offshore entities) and you should possess strong technical accounting skills, an aptitude for developing solutions for complex accounting issues and a passion for developing ideas which support ongoing process improvement programs. You should also possess the kind of energy & drive which will help you to manage competing priorities in a dynamic and growth focussed enterprise.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact James McBeath on 0438 825 651. Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.

job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
The Finance Manager leads the day-to-day finance function and is accountable for delivering reliable financial control, forward-looking commercial analysis and clear project performance reporting. The role combines the core responsibilities of financial control and management accounting in one senior operational position suited to PFIS’s current scale and project-based operating model.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer you will be responsible for ensuring the financial records are accurate and audit-ready, while also helping management understand project margins, cash flow, budgets, forecasts and the financial drivers of business performance. It is expected to operate as a practical business partner to the directors, project teams and operational leaders, not solely as a technical accounting role.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the operational finance function and establish clear priorities, deadlines and service standards.
  • Own the month-end and year-end close processes, including the close timetable, journals, cut-off and review signoffs.
  • Lead the annual budget process and coordinate assumptions with department and operations
  • Prepare the monthly management pack with concise commentary on revenue, gross margin, EBITDA, cash, working capital and key risks.
  • Translate accounting results into practical insights and recommendations for non-finance managers.
  • Provide department and cost-centre reporting that supports accountability for controllable expenditure.
  • Own the finance components of revenue recognition, WIP, contract assets and contract liabilities.
  • Coordinate monthly project financial reviews, including contract value, approved variations, costs to date, estimate to complete and estimate at completion.
  • Analyse project margin movements and ensure significant changes are supported, explained and escalated.

Experience & Qualifications

  • CA/CPA (or equivalent) with relevant tertiary qualifications.
  • Demonstrated experience owning month-end close, balance sheet control and management reporting in an SME or mid-market environment.
  • Hands-on budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis and cash flow forecasting experience.
  • Practical project accounting experience, including WIP, revenue recognition, contract positions and project margin analysis.
  • Experience supervising or managing finance staff and reviewing work prepared by others.
  • Strong Excel capability and experience working with cloud accounting systems and structured reporting workbooks.
  • Ability to communicate financial information clearly to directors, managers and operational staff.

For a confidential discussion and to obtain a copy of the role description, please contact Ian Quinn at Dean & Ling Executive on iquinn@deanling.com.au. Applications, including your resume and a synopsis of how your experience, abilities and knowledge are relevant to this role please submit via the Apply button.

Alternatively, visit www.deanling.com.au to submit your application

job.title: Geotechnical Engineer
job.description:
As a seasoned and specialised Senior Consultant, I collaborate with a wide array of D’n’C Civil Contractors, Engineering Consultancies, and public sector employers who are actively seeking talented Geotechnical Engineers and Engineering Geologist. Operating out of Brisbane, I service clients across Australia, connecting skilled professionals with opportunities that align with their expertise and career aspirations.

Given the unprecedented levels of activity in infrastructure, disaster relief, and Olympics-related projects, my clients are urgently seeking experienced and competent engineers at all levels. Whether you're looking to work with small, agile firms or large, established organizations in the private or public sector, I have roles that can match your ambitions. My clients prioritize their staff's well-being, ensuring projects are delivered to high standards and completed safely.

Currently, we are seeking Civil Engineers and Geotechnical Engineers at all levels. Depending on your experience and the specific needs of the client, your responsibilities could include:

  • Conducting Site Investigations and Analysis
  • Engaging in Design and Engineering tasks
  • Providing Project Management Support
  • Collaborating with Clients and Stakeholders
  • Ensuring Health, Safety, and Environmental Compliance
  • Team and Business Leadership

To be considered, you ideally possess the following qualifications and attributes:

  • A tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering and/or Geotechnical Engineering,
  • Local experience in Australia or New Zealand—though international candidates are also welcome to apply
  • Experience with and of the following:
  • site investigations, producing both factual and interpretive reports, and using industry-standard design software (e.g., PLAXIS, WALLAP, Slope/W)
  • Familiarity with DTMR/RMS/VicRoads specifications, including main road and technical standards
  • Design & estimating – piling, ground improvement or bulk earthworks
  • Project delivery – piling or ground improvement
  • A collaborative spirit, thriving in multicultural team environments
  • Exemplary communication skills, both written and verbal
  • A genuine passion for engineering and a drive to excel in your field

My clients are offering full-time, permanent roles with significant career progression opportunities. Depending on your experience, you can expect:

  • A competitive base salary plus superannuation ($100k - $220k plus super)
  • Additional benefits such as mileage reimbursement or vehicle allowances, depending on the role
  • Genuine learning and development opportunities that can pave the way for career advancement
  • The chance to work with a dedicated team of engineering professionals who take pride in their work and ensure everyone gets home safely at the end of the day

If the above resonates with you and you want to take the grunt work out of your job search, get in touch today for a confidential discussion. Please contact Justin Bindman at 0431 821 593 or via email at jbindman@deanling.com.au.

job.title: Assistant Company Secretary
job.description:
This well-established superannuation trustee, part of a growing investment group, is known for its professional, supportive and collaborative culture and its commitment to delivering long-term value for members. As the organisation continues to strengthen its governance framework and processes, they are seeking an Assistant Company Secretary to provide practical, high-quality governance and secretariat support to the trustee Board and its Committees. This is a fully remote role, open to candidates based anywhere in Australia.

Reporting to the Company Secretary, you will coordinate the full lifecycle of Board and Committee meetings, from annual calendars, agendas and paper collation through to minutes, resolutions and action item tracking. You will support a range of Committees, including Risk, Audit and Compliance, Investment, Membership Services and Nominations and Remuneration. You will also work closely with Chairs, Directors and executives to improve the quality, clarity and timeliness of Board papers. You will support the Director and Responsible Person lifecycle, including appointments, inductions, declarations, conflicts and offboarding, and will maintain governance registers and records using Diligent and related systems. In addition, you will assist with ASIC and APRA obligations and support cyclical governance reviews, including fit and proper, skills and Board performance assessments. You will also contribute to governance uplift projects that make processes simpler and more reliable.

You will be an experienced governance professional, currently working as an Assistant Company Secretary, Governance Officer or Board Secretariat specialist. Superannuation experience is strongly preferred, and you will bring a sound working knowledge of trustee governance and the APRA-regulated environment. You will hold a tertiary qualification in law, business, commerce, governance or a related discipline, or have equivalent relevant experience, and will hold or be working towards the Graduate Diploma in Applied Corporate Governance from the Governance Institute of Australia. With highly developed written and verbal communication skills, you will have a proven track record in preparing Board and Committee materials and taking minutes. You will have a sound understanding of the Corporations Act as it relates to the company secretarial function. Highly organised and meticulous in your attention to detail, you will take pride in getting things right and will be confident following up Directors and executives to keep meetings and decisions on track. You will also bring an interest in continuing your professional development in superannuation and trustee governance.

For a strictly confidential discussion, please contact Sarah Ling on 0402 265 217. Alternatively, submit your application (Word version) via the Apply button.
